name: Commercial leases and occupier management
one_line: The ESTATE-MANAGEMENT lifecycle of business premises after heads of terms are agreed: the schedule of condition recorded at the start, the rent-review and break machinery that runs mid-term, the licences to alter and to assign or sublet, the service-charge and insurance recharges, the rent-deposit and guarantee arrangements, and the dilapidations reckoning that settles what the premises must be handed back as. The anchor is ONE OCCUPIER'S TENANCY OF ONE PREMISES and the calendar of dates it created. Absorbs the legacy row prop.commercial-lease. Placeholder row (J-IND, researched to J-DEPTH): it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). What makes it a node is the ALIENATION, REVIEW AND BREAK machinery plus the lease-defined recharge proportion — the schedule of condition and the dilapidations schedule are shared with construction_property.survey-valuation and are not this row's exclusive fingerprint.

deterministic: PRECONDITION on every entry below: each is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. This template's schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so the material is recognised, kept local where the sensitivity setting says so, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a SCHEDULE OF CONDITION structure: a dated photographic and written record of the state of specific premises at the start of a term, organised room by room or elevation by elevation, prepared expressly to limit a future liability. The photographs plus the room-by-room narrative plus the stated purpose are the signal.

a DILAPIDATIONS structure: a schedule of breaches with a covenant reference, a remedy and a costed sum per item, summing to a claim, usually with a scott-schedule-style response column. It is SHARED with construction_property.survey-valuation, which names the same structure in its own recognition and owns it as a surveyor's product; this row detects it as a member of a tenancy, not as an opinion. Corrected in the deepening pass — the earlier claim that the structure exists nowhere else on the roster was wrong against that landed sibling. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
a RENT-REVIEW structure: a memorandum or notice recording a reviewed rent from a review date, with comparable evidence or an expert determination behind it, referenced to a lease and a premises.

an ALIENATION structure: a consent regime governing who may occupy — a licence to assign or sublet naming a proposed transferee, an authorised guarantee agreement by the outgoing tenant, a landlord's consent conditional on covenant strength. This regime has no counterpart in residential letting and no counterpart in an opinion document, and it is the signal this row stands on when the schedule of condition is conceded as shared.

a LEASE-EVENT CALENDAR structure: a schedule of dates derived from an instrument — term commencement, review dates, break dates and their notice periods, expiry — held to be diarised rather than to be read.
a LICENCE structure: a licence to alter, to assign or to sublet, referencing a headlease, describing works or a proposed transferee, and imposing reinstatement or covenant conditions.
a RECHARGE structure: a service charge or insurance rent apportionment for one commercial unit against a landlord's expenditure schedule, with a lease-defined proportion.
a SECURITY structure: a rent deposit deed with a stated sum and drawdown mechanics, or a guarantee or authorised guarantee agreement naming a guarantor.

a HEADS OF TERMS structure: a subject-to-contract summary of proposed lease terms — premises, term, rent, incentive, break, repairing obligation — expressly not binding, sitting immediately before the instrument.
a premises address in a labelled slot together with a lease or unit reference and a lease-derived DATE. Neither half fires alone.
parent-folder context naming a premises, a unit or a lease reference — a clue only, never firing alone.

a calendar entry whose SUMMARY names a rent review, a break date, a lease expiry or a rent quarter day, with a recurrence rule. “Calendar formats such as ICS should yield event title, start and end time, location, organizer, attendees, and recurrence metadata.” The CONTENT fires; calendar is a SOURCE_TYPE, not a domain.
needs_llm: an unlabelled document that reads as a lease, an agreement for lease, a licence, a tenancy at will or heads of terms — which one it is decides whether the protected legal side owns the file.
correspondence about a break notice, where whether it is a valid exercise, a query or a dispute changes both the group and the sensitivity.
deciding whether the holder is the landlord, the tenant, the managing agent or an adviser to one of them — the same schedule reaches all four and the role is what makes the file mean anything.
a photograph of a shopfront or an office interior with no caption: a schedule of condition image, a dilapidations image, a marketing shot or a fit-out record.
never_alone: a postal address or a street name alone — the family's constitutional never-alone, set by the construction_property schema row on 00's own reasoning about a university name: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” A premises address is on the lease, the licence, the recharge, the marketing particulars and the tenant's own letterhead.
a firm, practice, contractor, agency or authority name alone — same reasoning, same sentence. A tenant is an organisation, and an organisation name is the multi-role token 00 warns about.

a rent or premium figure alone. a money figure alone. Quotations, valuations, appraisals, service charges, rents, offers and appraisals all carry amounts, as does every other roster schema that touches money.

a signature or execution block alone. The landed legal.leases-agreements row makes this point repeatedly and it is adopted here unchanged: an execution block is shared with every signed instrument on the roster.
a lease-shaped clause structure alone — party recitals plus numbered covenants describe a loan agreement, an employment agreement, a service agreement and a licence equally well.

a document-type word alone (certificate, drawing, schedule, survey, valuation, report, plan, lease). Each is a work_type VALUE that appears in several worlds; the landed finance.household-property row carries title, inspection, warranty and completion certificate as its own work types.

a bare 4-digit number alone — 00 warns that file names and documents frequently contain numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values. Here they are also plot, drawing, valuation and unit numbers.

a source_type or extension alone. 00 requires that the engine “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and “Design and creative formats such as PSD, AI, SVG, Figma exports, CAD files, and 3D files should at minimum yield filename, format, dimensions or canvas properties, embedded metadata, layers or artboards where accessible, linked asset names, and preview text; unsupported proprietary formats should be recorded as indexed-but-unreadable rather than silently treated as empty.”
a download session alone. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

work_types: rent review notice, memorandum or determination
break notice and vacant possession record
licence to alter, assign or sublet
service charge or insurance rent recharge
rent demand, statement and arrears record
interim or terminal dilapidations schedule and response
settlement or completion record of a dilapidations claim
tenancy schedule or rent roll for a landlord's holdings
grouping_reasons: ONE TENANCY end to end — one occupier of one premises from heads of terms to expiry or surrender. The row's primary group and purpose-coherent across members that share nothing but the tenancy: “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one LEASE EVENT and everything around it: a rent review's notice, comparables, determination and memorandum; or a break's notice, correspondence and vacant-possession evidence.
one DILAPIDATIONS claim: the schedule, the photographs, the response, the negotiation and the settlement.
one PREMISES across successive occupiers over decades — the landlord's group, which outlives every tenancy and which is the reason this row follows the family's property-first default.

one landlord's portfolio at one moment: a tenancy schedule or rent roll, which is a group of PREMISES rather than of documents and which must not become a fact copied onto its members — “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one repeatedly re-exported engrossment or plan pack, joined by duplicate_family alone; “A content-hash match supports deduplication review; a filename match alone does not.”

no group at all is valid: a single licence to alter with nothing around it is a standalone record. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

and the stop rules apply: “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two units' papers in one building do not merge because they share a landlord and a service charge.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and construction_property declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row's open_question (NJ-CP-1). The recommendation, held as prose: the PREMISES first — the family default, and correct here because a shop or a floor outlives every occupier and the landlord's file is premises-keyed. Then the TENANCY, because one premises is let repeatedly and the tenancy is what separates the 2014 lease from the 2026 one. Then the document function (instrument / condition / review / licence / recharge / dilapidations). A period level is explicitly NOT recommended: this situation is event-driven rather than cyclical, and its dates are a diary, not a folder structure. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The row's defining boundary, stated as the reciprocal of the landed row, which already names the tenancy-packet fixture and the finance.household-property line. The landed row holds the OPERATIVE INSTRUMENT as the holder's own protected agreement record — party recitals, covenants, grant of occupancy, consideration, execution. This row holds the ESTATE-MANAGEMENT APPARATUS that runs a business tenancy after grant — schedule of condition, rent-review memorandum, licence, recharge, dilapidations schedule, lease-event diary. Premises address, rent amount and a signature block are shared observations and count for neither. legal is a safety schema and protects first, so where the instrument itself is in question the protected side leads. Where the role does not settle, neither activates: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.”

A residential tenancy and a commercial one produce parallel documents — an inventory beside a schedule of condition, a deposit beside a rent deposit deed, a check-out report beside a dilapidations schedule. The discriminating evidence is the OCCUPIER and the covenant regime: business premises with a repairing obligation, a contracting-out declaration, rent review and dilapidations apparatus support this row; a household's own record of the home it lives in or lets supports finance.household-property. A premises address and a rent count for neither. Where the role does not settle, neither activates: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.”

A tenant organisation's own occupation record overlaps this row exactly, and this is the collision most likely to fire on a real corpus, because most people holding these files are the TENANT. The discriminating evidence is whether the document manages the LEASE (review, break, licence, dilapidations, recharge — this row) or the WORKPLACE (desk allocation, access passes, cleaning rotas, moves — facilities-workplace). A premises address is on both.

Reciprocates the block-management row's edge. A per-unit recharge under one lease is this row; a whole-building budget with an apportionment schedule across all units is block-management. A service-charge line appears in both and decides neither.

Reciprocates the agency row's edge. Material made to FIND an occupier is agency-listing; material that runs the tenancy once granted is this row. A rent figure and a premises address count for neither.

The landed legal.leases-agreements row already states this pair from its side and the reasoning carries over unchanged: a lease's insurance-requirements clause and an insurance rent recharge report on insurance without being insurance. Labelled Named Insured, Policy Number, Policy Period and coverage tables support finance.insurance-corporate; a lease-defined recharge proportion supports this row.

RECIPROCATES the landed tenancy-management edge, which routes its commercial-lease collision fixture here, and adopts its discriminator unchanged rather than restating it differently: a deposit protection scheme, a right-to-rent check, prescribed information and a residential statutory notice support that row; a term of years, rent review provisions, alienation and dilapidations obligations support this one. Added in the deepening pass — the earlier draft deliberately withheld this edge while the sibling was unlanded. NOTE THE LINE THIS PAIR IS NOT DRAWN ON: that the tenant is a business is an organisation name, which is never-alone on this schema and cannot activate anything. The line is the COVENANT REGIME and the documents it produces — a contracting-out declaration, an upward-only review, an FRI repairing obligation, a licence to assign, an authorised guarantee agreement and a terminal dilapidations schedule have no residential counterpart, and deposit protection and safety certification have no commercial one. The privacy postures also differ and reinforce the split: that row's default residual is Protected Records because a named person lives there; this row's exposure is commercial confidence, with personal data entering mainly through individual guarantors. A mixed-portfolio landlord crosses the line constantly — NJ-CP-9.

RECIPROCATES the landed survey-valuation edge, and CONCEDES ground the earlier draft claimed. That row names the schedule of condition and the dilapidations schedule among its own deterministic signals, so those two structures are SHARED EVIDENCE and are not this row's exclusive fingerprint. The discriminator is that row's own: a labelled addressee, a stated purpose, a basis or standard, a limitation of liability and a professional indemnity statement make a RELIANCE document and support survey-valuation; a lease reference, a review or break date, an alienation consent and a lease-defined recharge proportion make TENANCY MACHINERY and support this row. Where a schedule of condition sits inside a tenancy file, both hold on disjoint evidence and neither is a file-level winner. Shared fixture, named on this side: Schedule of condition - 14 Foundry Row - Fenwick Surveyors.pdf.

RECIPROCATES the landed construction-project edge and adopts its discriminator unchanged: a fit-out is works under a building contract AND a tenant's obligation under a lease. Which INSTRUMENT the document serves decides it — an interim valuation, a contract instruction and a variation serve the building contract and support construction-project; a licence to alter, its reinstatement condition, the schedule of condition it was granted against and the dilapidations line it later produces serve the lease and support this row. The same fit-out drawings are referenced by number from both sides and discriminate nothing.

falls_through_to.why: Where the material carries an occupier's, tenant's or leaseholder's identity, or a commercially confidential figure, the protective home is correct. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The right home when the document is plainly real but its property, instruction or side is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The honest home for a standalone member of this situation with no accepted group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

A single site or property photograph with no event, job or set around it. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

Ordinary rather than exotic here: CAD and BIM formats recorded as indexed-but-unreadable, and password-protected data-room and tender exports. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

Isolated transactional members — a delivery note, a hire confirmation, a fee invoice with nothing around it. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

sensitivity_why: Predominantly commercial rather than personal, and recorded that way. The material states what a named business pays for its premises, what it owes, what security it gave and what liability it faces at expiry — commercially confidential to a counterparty who is usually not the user, and the sort of thing whose disclosure changes a negotiation. Personal data enters through named guarantors, who are frequently individuals giving personal guarantees, and through arrears correspondence. 00's corpus sentence covers the documents this situation accumulates — the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”. The cautious setting follows. The handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Four. (1) NJ-CP-9, row-specific and now RECIPROCATED rather than owed: the commercial/residential line against construction_property.tenancy-management, which landed after the first pass and routes its commercial fixture here. Both rows draw the line on the covenant regime and its documents, not on the tenant's legal form — an organisation name is never-alone on this schema and could not activate a row on its own. What stays open is the mixed-portfolio landlord whose corpus crosses the line inside one folder, and whether a corpus that shows a commercial regime and a residential one at the same address should activate both or neither. (2) NEW, and the most consequential thing this pass found: construction_property.survey-valuation names the schedule of condition and the dilapidations schedule among its OWN deterministic signals. The first pass called them structures that exist nowhere else on the roster and rested the node test on them; that was wrong against a landed sibling and is corrected here. They are shared evidence, split on the reliance structure, and this row now rests on the alienation, review and break machinery plus the lease-defined recharge proportion instead. R1c should confirm the split rather than let two rows claim one fingerprint. (3) Whether the lease-event diary is a filing situation at all or a P10/P11 concern: a schedule of dates held to be diarised is arguably a calendar rather than a record, and 00 is explicit that calendar is a SOURCE_TYPE and not a domain. This row keeps it as a work type and a detection structure and claims nothing about diarising. (4) Inherits NJ-CP-1: without a property key this row's recommended tree cannot be expressed as dimensions at all.
